tasks.notes: out-of-FILES: `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_exam_fix_edit.mjs` is edited by the diff but is absent from this task's Files block, and the Proof's own bullet calls that sim "unchanged: the fix round still runs in the task clone after the handoff". The edit was unavoidable and correct: that file's leg (c) pinned `row.examEdited === ['t1_test.sh']` for a FIRST-round implementer write at the Proof path, which M4 now defines as no edit at all, so the leg could not have stayed as written. The hunk narrows leg (c) to the half that outlived the change (reviewed and folded) and re-pins `examEdited` to `[]`; legs (a), (b) and (d) still pin the fix round's edit, so nothing is weakened and the divergence is disclosed in the file's own comment. The defect is the task text (Files omits the path, and the Proof asserts it unchanged), and the fix lies outside FILES — recorded, not blocking.; Stale comment inside this task's own FILES: `fleet/run-engine.mjs:87-88`, the EXAMINER_SCHEMA header, still reads "the wave-0 worker that writes the task's Proof tests in the task's own clone at BASE, before the implementer sees the tree" — the two facts M1 and M3 just replaced. Every other comment on the path (the exam block, the handoff, `defaultCloneNameOf`) was rewritten; this one was missed.; Same stale claim outside FILES, where this diff cannot fix it: `fleet/run-worker.mjs:157-159` documents the examiner role as writing "in the task's own clone at BASE, so its writable root is the implementer's — the same tree, before the implementer sees it". The behaviour it justifies (`writableRoot: 'clone'`) is still correct, since the confine hook's root is the worker's cwd and `makeCwdFor` now answers `exam-<id>` — only the sentence is wrong. `fleet/run-worker.mjs` is in no task's Files block, so this is recorded for the operator rather than routed to a fix round.; The handoff copies the examiner's BYTES but not its file MODE when the implementer already created a file at the Proof path. `fs.copyFileSync` (fleet/run-engine.mjs:1014) opens an existing destination with O_TRUNC, so the destination keeps the mode the implementer gave it; git then records the implementer's mode (100644 vs 100755) in the re-captured patch and the fold. Harmless for the `bash <script>` / `node <file>` / `pytest` test commands in use, but it is the one byte of "the peer's exam wins at the Proof path" that the substrate does not enforce. Removing the destination first makes the copy create the file with the examiner's mode.; unverified: acceptance is `suite — the committed suite is the verification`, but the evidence covers the eight Proof `Run:` sims, this task's exam, and `tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py` — not the whole gate (`python3 -m pytest`, which bridges every `fleet/tests/test_*.mjs` via `tests/test_fleet_suite.py`). Reading the tree closes most of the gap: every sim that dispatches an examiner (`proofTests` non-empty) is one of the eight already green, non-exam sims take the BASE path unchanged (with `examBlobs` null, the deleted `noteDrift('the implementer')` was a no-op and `'examEdited' in row === false` still holds, as `test_run_engine_proof_runs.mjs:176,431` require), `test_exam_dispatch_role.mjs`'s source regex still matches the new `label: 'exam:' + task.id … EXAMINER_SCHEMA` dispatch, and nothing globs `<patchesDir>` (the fold is handed `impl.patch` by name), so the new `exam-<id>.patch` is inert. What would settle it is one full `python3 -m pytest` on this tree.; Out-of-FILES edit, and the task text calls that file unchanged: the diff modifies `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_exam_fix_edit.mjs` (leg (c), lines 162-194), which is not in the Files block and which the Proof describes as "the fix-round edit sim, unchanged". The edit itself is necessary and correct — leg (c) pinned `row.examEdited === ['t1_test.sh']` for a first round that writes at the Proof path, and under M4 that value is now `[]`, so the sim could not have stayed unchanged and still passed. The defect is the task's own text: the Context's "Deletion owed" list and the Files block both omit this sim. The divergence is disclosed in the file's own comment ("Since #653 there is nothing for it to record either…") and the Run: bullet for it exits 0, so nothing here blocks; the path that has to change is the task's Files block, which is outside this tree. This also trips the prose GLOBAL CONSTRAINT "No file outside a task's own Files block is edited", which carries no `Check:` the driver ran.; The handoff loses the examiner's file mode when the implementer already created the Proof path. `fleet/run-engine.mjs` copies with `fs.copyFileSync(path.resolve(examDir, p), dest)` over an existing `dest`; libuv passes the source mode only to the *creating* `open`, so an existing destination keeps the implementer's mode. That is exactly leg (c)'s shape (the implementer writes its own `t1_test.sh`, the peer's bytes are laid over it): the content is the peer's but the executable bit is the submitter's, and the re-captured `task-<id>.patch` records that mode. Harmless for an exam invoked as `bash t1_test.sh` — which is why the sim does not catch it — and wrong for one the test command executes directly. Unlinking before the copy makes the handed-in file the examiner's in mode as well as bytes.; A file the examiner wrote outside `proofTests` is now silently lost. The handoff in `fleet/run-engine.mjs` copies only the recorded `proofTests` paths, so a fixture or helper the exam imports stays behind in `exam-<id>` and the exam goes red in the graded clone for a reason that reads as the implementer's fault (a red pre-review pass burns the one repair round, then `proof-red`). At BASE the examiner wrote into the graded clone, so such a file survived by construction. `fleet/roles/examiner.md` step 2 ("Write only the file(s) the Proof `Test:` slot names") makes this the examiner's rule rather than a hole, and that file is byte-pinned here — but the loss is currently invisible. The examiner's own capture at `<patchesDir>/exam-<id>.patch` already names every path it touched; one `judgmentCalls.push` when that set exceeds `proofTests` would make a dropped fixture readable in the run report instead of arriving as an unexplained red exam.; unverified: `CLAUDE.md:155` still states the #551 map's rule as "the implementer runs the peer's exam", which this change makes false — the implementer works in a clone the exam never enters, and the first party to run it is the driver's pre-review pass (then the fix round). `CLAUDE.md` is outside this task's FILES and is not one of the four documents `tests/test_docs_agree_with_code.py` gates (that test covers SKILL, FIRST_RUN, `fleet/RUNBOOK.md`, `README.md`, and it exited 0), so nothing here blocks and no edit inside this tree answers it. Operator-visible phase label regression: `phase('Depth-1 Leg')` (fleet/run-engine.mjs, inside `runShallowLeg`) is now immediately superseded by `phase('Integration Review')` (first line of `runCritic`), because `Promise.all([runShallowLeg(), runCritic()])` starts the leg, which yields at its first `await` on the clone, and then the critic sets the phase. No test or doc pins either string (grep across the tree finds only the two `phase(...)` call sites), so a single combined label emitted once before the barrier — e.g. `phase('Integration Review + Depth-1 Leg')` outside both closures, dropping the two inner calls — restores the signal without changing any pin. The submission diverges correctly and discloses it: `criticFindings()` in fleet/tests/test_run_engine_depth1_beside_critic.mjs:29-33 reads `report.review.findings` when present and falls back to `report.completenessFindings`, with a comment naming the BASE line, so the legs still pin the finding rather than a field name. 'engine-recsubject-')`) and never removes it, so two full engine runs (clones, patches, run dir) are left in $TMPDIR after the sim passes. The sim named as the shape in Context, `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_reconcile.mjs`, does clean up (`fs.rmSync(tmp, {recursive: true, force: true})` at its end); `test_run_engine_fold_subject.mjs`, whose plan-file shape was copied, does not. completenessFindings.detail: Footprint escape against the plan's global constraint "No file outside a task's own Files block is edited": `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_exam_fix_edit.mjs` was edited in this run, but it is not in Task 1's Files block (which lists run-engine.mjs, run-waves.mjs, roles/implementer.md, roles/fix.md, and the four sims examiner/exam_edits/exam_edited_patches/exam_evidence, plus the new exam_together test), and Task 1's Proof bullet explicitly describes it as "the fix-round edit sim, unchanged". Its leg (c) now carries post-#653 prose and assertions that cannot have existed at BASE af1e7c7 — the comment at lines 165-171 reads "Since #653 there is nothing for it to record either: the implementer never holds the exam, so its own file at the Proof path is overwritten by the peer's bytes at the handoff", and line 191 asserts `row.examEdited` deep-equals `[]` "the handoff put the peer's bytes there". At BASE this leg pinned the opposite (the implementer's first-round edit being recorded), so the edit was substantively necessary once Task 1's handoff landed — the defect is that the plan declared the file unchanged and left it out of the Files block, so the change was made outside the declared scope and no referee read it against a contract that admitted it. The edit itself is correct and the sim is green in the integrated run evidence, so this is worth an issue against the plan's scoping (Task 1 Files/Proof slots) rather than a stop on the merge.
